message.reasoning:
We need to analyze constraints.

Variables: P,Q,R,S each T/F (on/off). Exactly two are on.

Rules:
1. If P is on, Q is on. (P -> Q)
2. If Q is on, R is off. (Q -> not R)
3. S is on iff exactly one of P and R is on. So S = (P XOR R). Means S true iff (P != R). Equivalent to (S ↔ (P ⊕ R)).

We need a statement that must be true in every configuration satisfying these rules. Options: A: P and Q are both on. B: R and S are both on.

Check possibilities.

Let's enumerate possibilities respecting exactly two on.

Let’s consider cases.

We can brute think.

Let’s denote truth values.

We need exactly two true among {P,Q,R,S}.

Constraint1: If P true then Q true, so P true forces Q true. That would already give at least two true (P and Q). Could be exactly those two, with R,S false. Must also satisfy other constraints.

Constraint2: If Q true then R false. So in case P true => Q true => R false. So R must be false.

Constraint3: S = (P XOR R). Since R false, S = P XOR false = P. So S = P.

Thus if P true, then S true as well. But then we would have P true, Q true, S true (three true) contradict exactly two true. So P cannot be true. Therefore P false.

Thus P = false.

Given P false, rule1 (P -> Q) is vacuously satisfied; Q can be either.

Rule3: S = (P XOR R) = (false XOR R) = R. So S = R.

Thus S and R have same truth value.

Now we have exactly two true among Q,R,S (since P false). And R=S.

Let’s consider possibilities:

Case 1: R = S = true. Then they are both true (2 true). Q must be false to keep exactly two true. Check rule2: If Q true then R false. Q is false, so rule2 satisfied. So configuration: P=F, Q=F, R=T, S=T works. Exactly two true (R,S). S = R satisfied. Good.

Case 2: R = S = false. Then they are both false, need exactly two true, so Q must be true and also need another true, but only P is false. So we need exactly two true; currently Q true, others false, that's only one true. Not allowed. So R=S cannot both be false.

Thus the only viable configuration is R=S=true, Q false, P false.

Thus must have R and S both on, and P and Q off.

Hence statement B (R and S are both on) must be true. A is false.

Answer: B.
